findings.title: Hung spawned flusher is never killed; its replacement runs alongside it
findings.description:
In `_ensure_processes_alive`, `process.kill()` runs only inside `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):`. Production creates processes via `self.mp_context.Process` with the `spawn` context, which yields a `SpawnProcess`. In CPython, `SpawnProcess` and `Process` are sibling subclasses of `BaseProcess` (`multiprocessing/context.py:220` and `:284` in 3.12; same layout in 3.13), so the check is `False` and `kill()` is skipped. The removed code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this is a regression.

When a process is flagged `hang`, it is still alive. The replacement starts on the same shards (line 259), and the old process keeps running until the parent exits, since `daemon=True` only ends it then. Both processes can call `buffer.flush_segments` on the same queue keys and produce the same segment to `buffered-segments` twice. The old process also keeps writing the shared `healthy_since` value.

`join()` has the same wrong guard (lines 346-347), so `terminate()` never runs for spawned processes. That predates this diff, but the diff copies the pattern into more code.

Fix: use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` in both places, and add a test that forces a restart with a spawned process.

findings.title: The added `time.sleep` in `test_basic` is a no-op
findings.description: `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15. `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 resolves on the same `time` module, so it returns immediately. The comment "Give flusher threads time to process" is therefore wrong, and the test still races: it can call `step.join()`, which sets `stopped`, before the flusher thread flushes after the drift change. The added `step.poll()` does not change that ordering. Wait on the observable result with a deadline, or capture a real sleep before the patch, as `test_flusher.py` does with `from time import sleep`.

findings.title: No test covers the process path; the new test checks internals
findings.description: `test_flusher_processes_limit` passes `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, so `SpanFlusher` uses `threading.Thread` (flusher.py:106-108), not the spawn path production uses. The regression above is invisible to the suite. The test asserts `len(processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and a total shard count (lines 114-121). These are internals and do not show that each process gets the correct shards or that its buffer is scoped to them. No test exercises `_ensure_processes_alive` with more than one process, and none covers the `flusher_processes=None` default.

findings.title: Memory check repeats cluster-wide Redis INFO calls per buffer
findings.description: `submit` now calls `buffer.get_memory_info()` once for each entry in `self.buffers`. That method returns `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:375-376`), which queries the whole cluster (`cluster.info()`, `src/sentry/processing/backpressure/memory.py:86-88`). With N flusher processes, each `submit` makes N cluster-wide round trips and appends N identical copies of every node's memory. The `used / available` ratio stays correct only because every copy is identical. Query once from the parent instead.

findings.title: Dead method `_create_process_for_shard`
findings.description: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) has no callers. `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. The two names differ by one letter, which invites confusion. Remove the singular method.

findings.title: `--flusher-processes` accepts 0 and negative values
findings.description: The option is `type=int` with no lower bound. In `flusher.py:51`, `max_processes or len(...)` turns `0` into one process per shard without any warning. A negative value passes through `min()` at line 60, `range(num_processes)` becomes empty, and `process_to_shards_map[process_index]` at line 66 raises `KeyError` during construction. Use `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

findings.title: The `shard` metric tag means different things across metrics
findings.description: `flusher_unhealthy` (lines 243-245) tags `shard` with a single integer. `flusher.produce` (line 185) and `segment_size_bytes` (lines 192-196) tag `shard` with the comma-joined list of all shards the process owns, for example `"0,1,2,3"`. `wait_produce` (line 199) uses the plural key `shards`. A dashboard filtering on `shard:3` will miss the produce metrics whenever a process owns more than one shard. Pick one key and one meaning.

findings.title: Docstring and defaults disagree
findings.description: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard." The CLI default (`consumers/__init__.py:434`, `default=1`) produces one flusher process in total, while the factory default of `None` produces one per shard. The `:param` list also omits `max_processes`. Document the actual default, and either align the CLI and factory defaults or state why they differ.

findings.title: `max-flush-segments` now applies per flusher process
findings.description: `flush_segments` derives its per-shard cap from `len(self.assigned_shards)`, and each process now has a buffer with only its own shards. With the default `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments=500`, each process can flush about 500 segments per cycle, so the total is roughly 500 × `flusher_processes`, where it used to be 500 overall. This may be intended, but the option is not documented as per-process, and Redis and Kafka load now scales with the new flag. Confirm and document it.

findings.title: Two `num_processes` attributes mean different things in one pipeline
findings.description: `SpanFlusher.num_processes` is the flusher process count. `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.num_processes` (`factory.py:51`) is the batch-processing pool size. Both sit in the same pipeline and share a name with different meanings. Consider `num_flusher_processes` for the flusher.

findings.title: The CLI option reaches the factory under the same name
findings.description: `cmd_context.invoke(strategy_factory_cls, **cmd_context.params, ...)` passes `flusher_processes` as a keyword. That matches the new parameter in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` (`factory.py:41`), which forwards it as `max_processes=` to `SpanFlusher` (`factory.py:74`).
